Fit the declared model with rms

Source: R/modeling_rms.R
mm_model.Rd

Builds the formula from the project, fits it with rms::lrm(), and keeps everything a later step needs: the fit, its datadist, the formula it was actually given, a prediction schema and a fingerprint of the coefficients.

Usage

mm_model(
  project,
  cohort,
  nonlinear = NULL,
  interactions = NULL,
  knots = NULL,
  check_leakage = TRUE
)

Arguments

project

A mm_project() configuration.

cohort

The development data. When the project declares a split, only rows below split_at are used, and the held-out rows are returned untouched for later scoring.

nonlinear

Continuous predictors to fit with restricted cubic splines. NULL takes the project's prespecified nonlinear, which is where the choice belongs. Supplying it here overrides the plan and the departure is recorded on the returned object and warned about, because a model whose shape differs from the written plan is a finding and not a detail.

interactions

Prespecified interaction blocks. NULL takes the project's, with departures recorded the same way.

knots

Knots for each spline term. NULL takes the project's.

check_leakage

Scan the development predictors for duplication of the outcome. TRUE for a declared model. mm_full_process() passes FALSE when refitting inside a resample, because the declared cohort has already been scanned and a resample is a subset of it, so a match there is a property of the draw rather than of the analysis. It is not an override: there is no way to reach it with a cohort that has not been scanned.

Value

An object of class mm_model.

Details

x and y are kept on the fit, because validation and calibration need them and a fit without them fails later for reasons that do not name this decision. That is the only patient-level retention: the design matrix the model was fitted on and the outcome it was fitted to.

Nothing else of the cohort survives, and the mechanism is worth naming because the default behaviour is the opposite. A formula keeps the environment it was built in, rms::lrm() stores that environment on fit$terms and fit$sformula, and a formula built in this function's own frame would hold the cohort, the development rows and the split. The identifier column in particular is in none of them, so a saved model cannot carry patient identifiers into a place the data was never meant to go. The formula is built in baseenv() to keep that true.

A predictor that reproduces the outcome is refused. A model given its own outcome under another name reports near-perfect discrimination, which reads as success, and the by-name check that outcome is not among predictors cannot see a renamed copy. Separation that is not duplication is reported instead of refused, because in a small cohort it can be real. See mm_leakage(), including what it cannot tell you.

Strong hierarchy is enforced rather than assumed: an interaction is refused unless both of its main effects are in the project's predictors. The specification requires that an interaction only be usable with its constituent main effects, and a formula is the last place to find out.

Which rows are modelled is decided once, before anything is fitted, and the datadist, the fit and the prediction schema are all built from that one frame. rms would otherwise drop a row with a missing model variable at fit time, leaving three parts of the same object describing three different samples: the fit estimated on the complete rows, the schema taking its ranges and levels from the supplied ones, and the datadist taking the limits that set a nomogram's drawn axis. A value no fitted row carried then came back labelled as interpolation, and the printed nomogram reached values the model was never estimated on.

The difference is reported rather than absorbed, as n_supplied, n_incomplete and incomplete_by, and warned about. It matters most for the sample-size gate, which would otherwise judge a sample larger than the one that exists and so be most lenient exactly where it should be strictest. Deciding the analysis sample belongs in mm_clean(), where the exclusion reaches the flow diagram, not in na.action.

A factor level carried only by dropped rows is removed and named in lost_levels. It has no rows left to estimate it from, rms answers one with a singular Hessian whose message identifies neither the variable nor the level, and leaving it in the schema would let mm_predict() admit a level the model cannot score.

Examples

cohort <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 1)
project <- mm_project("uds", "event",
                      c("age", "bmi", "sex", "prior_uti"),
                      cohort = cohort)
fit <- mm_model(project, cohort, nonlinear = "age",
                interactions = list(c("prior_uti", "sex")))
#> Warning: the development sample may be too small for this model: 300 rows is 1097 short of the 1397 a model of 7 parameter(s) needs at 9.3% prevalence for 90% shrinkage. Coefficients from a sample this size are expected to be overfitted; see the adequacy element of the returned object.
fit
#> <mm_model: uds>
#>   formula    .mm_y ~ rms::rcs(age, 4) + bmi + sex + prior_uti + prior_uti:sex
#>   developed  300 rows, 28 events
#>   parameters 7 non-intercept, 1097 short of the sample they need
#>   apparent C 0.7126
#>   fingerprint fba075b46006604c
